title: Drinking Water Operations and Regulatory Compliance
statusDescription: Pilot curriculum. Director approval is required before advertising approved drinking-water CEUs.
audience: Ontario drinking-water operators and supervisors preparing, reviewing or handing over operational evidence.
outcomes: Distinguish a legal requirement, a system authorization, a procedure and an observation.
Classify targets, alarms and applicable requirements without conflating them.
Reconcile sample identifiers across field, transfer and laboratory records.
Distinguish internal escalation from applicable external reporting.
Make an attributable correction while preserving the original observation.
Combine source applicability, data review and task ownership in one decision record.

modules.title: Build the compliance and responsibility map
modules.summary: Distinguish a legal requirement, a system authorization, a procedure and an observation. Assign a case task to a verified role and identify unresolved authority. Create a source register that another operator can independently check.

modules.title: Interpret control limits and conflicting measurements
modules.summary: Classify targets, alarms and applicable requirements without conflating them. Align observations by time, place, method and hydraulic context. Quantify missing evidence while maintaining a parallel protective response.

modules.title: Reconstruct sample identity and result history
modules.summary: Reconcile sample identifiers across field, transfer and laboratory records. Distinguish a report amendment from evidence that the original result was invalid. Document sampling uncertainty without suppressing potentially significant results.

modules.title: Manage reporting, corrective action and closure as separate tasks
modules.summary: Distinguish internal escalation from applicable external reporting. Build a communication record showing attempts, contacts and directions. Specify evidence-based closure criteria and accountable follow-up.

modules.title: Correct records and reconstruct an audit trail
modules.summary: Make an attributable correction while preserving the original observation. Distinguish event time, entry time, instrument time and receipt time. Produce a coherent evidence index and identify misleading summaries.

modules.title: Defend a complete incident file
modules.summary: Combine source applicability, data review and task ownership in one decision record. Revise a conclusion when new evidence arrives without rewriting the past. Defend a proportionate closure recommendation using an explicit rubric.

completionRequirements: Participate in all 6 modules with instructor-verified attendance and engagement; 10 learning hours are planned, pending a timed pilot.
Pass each module check and submit every practical assignment for acceptance against all marking criteria.
Score at least 80% on the 12-question final assessment. Three attempts are available before instructor reassessment review.
Submit a course evaluation. An authorized instructor verifies completion and issues a non-credit pilot learning record.
publicDisclosure: Duration is a planning estimate, not earned credit. The flagship is planned over two five-hour days, excluding breaks. No approved CEUs or regulatory recognition are awarded. Director approval is required before any approved drinking-water CEU claim. Use current facility procedures and applicable requirements for operational decisions.

modules.title: Follow water and mass through the treatment train
modules.summary: Convert flow, concentration and mass loading consistently. Align samples with hydraulic travel and sampling delay. Distinguish an operating target from a validated treatment requirement.

modules.title: Characterize a changing source and set test priorities
modules.summary: Interpret turbidity with temperature, alkalinity and organic indicators. Select representative sampling and comparison periods. Prioritize evidence that discriminates between competing explanations.

modules.summary: Define success and stop criteria before a trial. Separate observed improvement from causal attribution. Prepare a cross-barrier review and handover.
